subject: ARPA Funding Update and Community Survey Results
overview: The administration presented an update on the allocation of American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds and reviewed results from a community survey used to prioritize future spending. The meeting focused on the remaining $19.7 million in grant funding and upcoming applications for nonprofit and housing support.

items.title: Opening and Introduction
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn introduced city staff and the purpose of the meeting to review the city's progress in distributing federal ARPA funds.

items.title: Community Survey Results Presentation
items.summary: Lorena Escalero reported that 416 respondents identified water and sewer improvements, green spaces, and social services as the top priorities for remaining ARPA funds.

items.title: Review of Current ARPA Allocations
items.summary: Staff reviewed completed and approved projects including health equity staffing, park and pool renovations, and infrastructure projects like sewer lining and water meter replacements.

items.title: Future Spending Forecast and Revenue Replacement
items.summary: The administration outlined a plan to allocate approximately $19.7 million toward nonprofit grants, infrastructure, and revenue replacement to sustain city and school staff salaries.

items.title: Public Comment and Q&A
items.summary: Participants discussed potential premium pay for first responders, accessibility enhancements for infrastructure, and funding for Medford Housing Authority developments.
